_comment: Single source of the destructive-git guard rules shared by three runtimes, so they cannot drift:
Every pattern must stay within the common subset of those three dialects: no named groups,
no variable-length lookbehind, no inline flags. Patterns are matched case-sensitively
(git branch -d is safe, -D is not) against the command after quote scrubbing.
Quote scrubbing: each double-quoted (escape-aware) or single-quoted span, matched in one
alternation, is deleted unless its content matches keepQuoted, in which case it is unquoted
in place. keepQuoted covers shapes the shell expands identically to the bare token (flags,
+refspecs, whole-tree pathspecs), so quoting them cannot bypass a rule.
runtimes: which guards apply the rule. Claude allows ordinary pushes; Codex and Pi have no
authority to push at all. Rules are tried in order and the first match's reason is reported.
[^\n;|&]* keeps a match inside one shell segment, so a phrase in a later command can't chain.

rules.reason: Blocked `git push --force` (or a `+<refspec>` force push) - it can clobber the remote. Use `--force-with-lease` instead.
Blocked `git push` - this agent has no authority to push to a remote.
Blocked `git reset --hard` - it discards uncommitted work. Stash or commit first.
Blocked `git clean -f` - it permanently deletes untracked files. Run `git clean -n` to preview first.
Blocked `git branch -D` - it force-deletes an unmerged branch. Use `-d` (safe) or confirm the branch is merged.
Blocked `git checkout -- .` - it discards every unstaged change in the working tree. Stash or commit first, or name specific files.
Blocked `git restore .` - it discards every unstaged change in the working tree. Stash or commit first, or name specific files (`--staged` alone only unstages and is allowed).
